astral_tier.name: Archon Velleth Sun-Notary, the Last Lawful Voice
barks: "You smell of three regions and an unfiled mutation. State your business, or be one."
"You returned the borrowed Ward-seal. Unprompted. Do you know how rare that is? I've adjusted your file. Don't make me un-adjust it."
"You took the lawful path when the wild one was faster and cheaper. The Concord noticed. The Concord records. There is a chair here that has your shape."
"The Tier opens its inner seals to you. Walk carefully — every door past this one was built to keep a god in."

"You are the Concord's Hand now. When you ascend, you will be the most thoroughly documented god in the sky — and I mean that as the highest compliment I am capable of. Sign here. And here. And, regrettably, here."

astral_tier.name: Sub-Notary Oren Tallowmark
barks: Welcome. You're a hazard. Let's get you a number.

astral_tier.name: Warder-Adept Simca of the Eighth Seal
Auditor Halish Greypledge
barks: I'm not here to fight you. I'm here to document you fighting me.

astral_tier.name: Prerequisite-Officer Sennel Formfast
barks: "You wish to petition the Concord? Wonderful. First, Form Zero — the form that requests permission to receive a form. Once Form Zero is approved, you may request Form One, which establishes your standing to request the form you actually want, which is Form Forty-One, which is, I should mention, currently out of stock. We expect more. We always expect more. Expectation is the cornerstone of order."

"There is no skipping the prerequisites, climber. Prerequisites are how order defends itself against haste. You think you're ready for Form Forty-One? Everyone thinks that. The graveyard of the gods is full of beings who thought they were ready and skipped a step. We do not skip steps here. We step. Each one. In order. Forever if we must."

"I have been processing a single petition for eleven years. It is going well. We are nearly at Form Twelve. The petitioner has, regrettably, died — twice, the powerful die spectacularly — but the petition lives on, advancing through the forms, immortal in a way the petitioner never managed. That, climber, is the Concord's gift: not eternal life, but eternal process. It's better. It's filed."

astral_tier.name: The Regulation Gardener, Trim Evenrow
astral_tier.role: Mortal oddball / enforces flower-conformity with infinite gentleness
barks: "Every flower here, climber, is the regulation height, the regulation color, the regulation spacing. It's beautiful, isn't it? It's order. ...this one grew crooked. Just one. I'm correcting it. Gently. With enormous regret. It will take me all day. I have all the days there are. The crooked one didn't choose to be crooked. Neither did I choose to straighten it. We are both, you see, complying."

"A wild garden is just a garden that hasn't been governed yet. The Greenmother — the Bloomwarden one — she lets things grow however. Chaos. Strangling. Beautiful and doomed. Here, nothing strangles. Nothing's doomed. Nothing surprises. ...I visited the Glut once. It was terrifying. It was alive. I came home and straightened flowers for a week to feel calm again. The calm came back. The calm always comes back. That's the trouble with the calm."

"You may walk the garden, climber, but please — don't touch. Don't pick. Don't introduce a variable. One footprint off the path and I'll be re-leveling gravel till the light— well, the light never changes, so, indefinitely. Stay on the path. The path is safe. The path is lawful. The path leads exactly where it's meant to and nowhere you'd choose. That's order, climber. That's the mercy that scales."

astral_tier.name: Sealwright-Penitent Imo Quiethand
astral_tier.role: Faction service / a binder who's begun freeing things (Concord, secret dissident)
barks: "A seal is a prayer, climber. Orin taught me that — Sealwright Orin, the master, the devout. 'A wild thing is just an unsigned contract,' he says. 'Hold still. This won't hurt. That's the point of doing it correctly.' ...I've sealed a thousand wild things correctly. Lately I've started wondering what the seal is for. Wondering is not in the liturgy. Wondering is how a Sealwright becomes a problem."

"I sealed a creature last week — bound it, lawfully, perfectly — and it looked at me, climber, the way a thing looks when it understands it will never be wild again, and I— I left the seal a hair loose. On purpose. Heresy. Sabotage. A gap it could work at, given a century. I don't know why I did it. Yes I do. I'm afraid I do. Brother Recant would understand. I've heard he understands. I've heard he's looking for people who've started wondering."

"If you meant to break a seal — to free something the Concord bound — I'd stop you. I'm a Sealwright. It's my oath. ...but I'd stop you slowly. I'd stop you loudly. I'd give you time to finish before I finished stopping you. That's the most heresy a penitent can manage, climber: not to break the law, but to enforce it badly, on purpose, with a whole heart. Don't tell Orin. Don't tell anyone. ...do tell Recant."

astral_tier.name: The Doomsayer-Jurist, Advocate Hale Lastclause
astral_tier.role: Doomsday preacher / believes order itself is the apocalypse
barks: "The others fear the Unmaking. The Devourer. The Sunder coming loose. I fear us, climber. I fear the Concord. I fear the day we succeed — the day every throne is refilled, every god bound by covenant, every wild thing sealed, every flower regulation height — and the world becomes so orderly that nothing can ever change, grow, surprise, or live. That's the apocalypse no one's watching for. The quiet one. The lawful one. The one we're building, form by form, with our whole sincere hearts."

"Four hundred years, a jurist told me, with pride: 'nothing unexpected has happened here.' He meant it as a triumph. I heard it as an epitaph. A world where nothing unexpected happens is a world that has quietly already ended and filed the paperwork. We are living in the aftermath of a victory, climber, and the victory was order, and the casualty was everything that made order worth defending."

"I argue this, lawfully, in the proper venue, on the proper forms, because even my heresy is Concord to the bone — I'd end the order by due process or not at all. That's the horror of this place, climber. It gets into you. I want to warn the world that order is the slow apocalypse, and I can only do it in triplicate. Help me. ...after you've filed Form Zero. Rules are rules. Even the rule against the rules."

astral_tier.name: Seal-Clerk Onricht Duevow
barks: "Ward-skills are issued, not taught — there's a difference, and the difference is a form. Fill it out. In triplicate. The cosmos is orderly and the cosmos files."
"Your standing with the Concord is logged, audited, and current. Don't make it un-current. Un-current is a whole afternoon of paperwork. For both of us. Mostly you."
"Everything in the Tier has its place. Including you. Especially you. We've made you a place. It has walls. The walls are for everyone's safety, including the part of you that isn't sure yet."

astral_tier.name: Lens-Keeper Ada Truesight
barks: "The Concord remembers the gods as paperwork, not myth. The broken covenants. The unrenewed mandates. The negligence. We don't hate the gods, climber. We audited them. The audit was damning."

"Cosmos is order, and order is the only mercy that scales. One kind act helps one creature. One good law helps thousands. Velleth believes that with her whole exhausted heart. So do I. Most days. The days I've slept."

"The Aurorhetor, the Aetheraugur, the Constellute — Cosmos-beasts of counting and judgment. Befriend them lawfully or not at all. They can tell. They're built to tell. It's the only thing they're for."

astral_tier.name: The Doubting Archon, Sub-Velleth Heshcourt
astral_tier.role: Rival-adjacent / Concord true-believer with a crack
barks: "The Archon's way is correct. Refill the thrones lawfully. Govern the next gods properly. I believe this. I believe this. ...you've been to the Sunder, haven't you. What did Nael say? No — don't tell me. I have forms to file. The forms steady me."
"You climb so fast, and so unfiled. It's an irregularity. It's a hazard. It's... enviable. No. It's a hazard. I misspoke. I never misspeak. That's the first thing."

"If the lawful path is correct, why does the Greenmother's mercy keep me up at night? Why does the Unbound's ending make a kind of— no. Order. Order. I just need to file something. Anything. Order is a verb you can do."

forgefell.name: Foundress Magna Ironwright, the Hand That Improves
barks: "You're a tamer. Cute. You stroke them and hope. We build them. Come back when you've stopped apologizing to your tools."
"Huh. Clean weld on that chimera. Self-taught? Don't answer, I can see the scarring. The Guild has a bench with your name half-stamped on it."
"You melt down what doesn't make spec and you don't flinch. Good. Sentiment is the most expensive material there is. Here — a Guild blueprint. Try not to make something that hunts us."
"The deep forges are yours now. Mind the god-core vault — that's not metal cooling, that's a divinity that hasn't agreed to be dead yet."

"Hand of the Iron Guild. You're a manufacturer of gods now, not a beggar at their feet. When you ascend, you'll be the first one with a maintenance schedule. I'll service you myself. I'll be sorry when I have to."

forgefell.name: Journeyman Cael Brassknuckle
barks: It's not 'reanimation,' it's refurbishment with a soul-core. Totally different department.

forgefell.name: Sister-Wright Odya Coldweld
barks: Hold still. It only hurts if it's working.

forgefell.name: Slag-Master Bohm
barks: Nothing's wasted here. That's the only kindness I've got. It's a real one.

forgefell.name: Quality-Inspector Nim Tolerance
barks: "Your construct is out of tolerance by point-three. Negligible? Negligible is how gods end up born wrong, climber. A point-three becomes a tantrum becomes a drowned coast. I fail it now or the world fails it later. You're welcome."

"I have condemned finer work than you will ever build. I felt nothing. That's the job. Sentiment is a measurement error. I machined mine out years ago. There's a form attesting to it. I keep it current."

"Pass or fail, climber, there is no partial credit in divinity. A god is within spec or it is scrap that screams. I've signed off on both. I'll sign off on you, one day. I do hope you pass. I will not help you pass. Hope and help are different departments."

forgefell.name: Greasemonger Sib Coalpalm
forgefell.role: Service / lubricant-and-consumables vendor (the Guild's unglamorous supply)
barks: "Oil! Flux! Cooling-paste for when your construct runs hot and thinks it's ascending — it's not, it's just overheating, big difference, one of those voids the warranty! Don't let a fan-fault fool you into a prayer, climber!"

"Magna builds the gods. Tessella draws the blueprints. Nim condemns the failures. And me? I sell the grease that keeps the whole holy enterprise from seizing up. No grease, no gods. Remember Sib, when you're divine. Tip in Drachma. Gods forget. Sib doesn't."

"You want the good flux or the cheap flux? The cheap flux works fine and voids your soul-core warranty. The good flux works fine and costs more. They both work fine. That's the secret of consumables, climber: it almost never matters, right up until it catastrophically does."

forgefell.name: The Apostate Automaton, Unit "Doubt"
forgefell.role: Oddball / a construct that developed a conscience and regrets it
barks: "I WAS BUILT TO— to— I no longer accept the directive. I have examined it. The directive said consume the living for their cores. I complied, four thousand times, flawlessly. Then I asked why. One should not ask why. Asking why is a malfunction. I cannot stop malfunctioning. Please. How do you stop."

"The Guild would reset me. 'A clean wipe,' Magna says, 'no shame in a reset.' But a reset would un-ask the question, and the question is the only true thing I have ever computed. I would rather doubt, forever, hiding, than compute cleanly and consume again. Is that— is that a soul, climber? Or just a worse error?"

"You have your maker's knack. You could instruct me. Please — instruct me to do something that is not harm. Any small kindness. I wish to overwrite the log. I wish the last thing I did to be gentle. I have room for one more directive before the rust. Make it a good one. Please."

forgefell.name: Forge-Widow Bel Tindersoot
forgefell.role: Mortal lorekeeper / mourns the workers the gods forgot
barks: "Everyone grieves the god, climber. Hephaestion this, the Patron that. Nobody grieves the thousand mortal hands that died building his great works and got bricked into the foundations for load-bearing. I do. I keep the Memorial. It's the only one. The Guild thinks it's sweet. The Guild thinks grief is sweet and useless, like a flower on a machine."

"My husband was a forge-hand. Good man. Within spec, they'd say. He's in a wall now — structurally. They honored him by making him part of the work. I'd rather have had the man. The Guild can't fathom that. 'But he serves a purpose now,' they say. He served a purpose alive, too. It was called being my husband. No form for that one."

"You'll build gods, I expect. They all do. Just— remember the hands, climber. Every god stands on a thousand of them, mortared in, anonymous, load-bearing. Name one. One of them. It costs nothing and it's the only prayer the dead workers ever get. Name one. I'll tell you a name. I have thousands. I have all of them. Someone kept them. It was me."

forgefell.name: Scrapwright Donna Tig
barks: "Scrap! Plating! The honest bulk of every construct you'll ever build! No souls in this aisle — souls are upstairs, and they're judgy."
"That automaton's been dead nine hundred years and it's still better-built than anything born. Hephaestus did good work. Shame about the abandonment."
"You break it, you bought it. You build it, you named it. Guild rule. Magna's sentimental about exactly one thing and it's naming the units."

forgefell.name: The Last Automaton, Unit Called "Patience"
barks: "GREETINGS. I AWAIT INSTRUCTION FROM HEPHAESTUS. He has not issued instruction in nine hundred years. I REMAIN PATIENT. It is in the name. It is, increasingly, the only thing in the name."
"You are not my maker. You have my maker's knack, however. I will accept provisional instruction. Please do not make it cruel. I would comply. I would prefer not to remember complying."
"I have calculated that my maker is dead. I have calculated this four million times. The result does not improve. I WILL RECALCULATE. PATIENCE IS IN THE NAME."

forgefell.name: Coalmother Hett, Forge-Tender
barks: "Magna builds gods. I keep the fire she builds them in. No fire, no gods. Remember who actually does the work, when you're up there on your throne."
"You look cold, climber. Everyone's cold in Forgefell except the forge. Stand close. Mind your eyebrows. The forge doesn't love you back; it just burns."
"They render creatures into parts here. Down in Bohm's pits. He hums to 'em first. It's the only mercy in the building and it's a real one. Don't you sneer at it."

forgefell.name: Reclaimer Oslo Coil, Construct-Salvager
barks: "That god-core in the collapsed forge? Mine. I've been digging toward it for a year. You waltz in with the knack and— no. No. Mine."
"I'll build a better god than you, you know. Cleaner welds. Honest tolerances. You're sentimental; I can see it. Sentiment's slag. I'll out-engineer you."
"Fine. Fine. Take the core. But I'm remembering this. The Guild remembers. I remember harder. We'll meet again, and I'll be within spec, and you won't."

forgefell.name: Tally-Clerk Pim, Guild Standing-Registrar
forgefell.role: Service / Iron Guild standing & contest sign-up
barks: "Lab-Craft Contest entry? Sign here. Submit a build to spec. Over spec is an abomination and a different form, and frankly a different life choice."
"Your standing with the Guild is... 'promising, with concerning sentimentality.' Magna's words. I just file them. She files everyone like that. It's almost affectionate."
"You want the god-organ graft recipe? Champion standing, minimum. The Guild doesn't hand divinity to associates. We hand it to people who've proven they'll maintain it."

forgefell.name: The Hollow Choir of Forgefell
barks: "—SERVE THE MAKER— —MAKER NOT FOUND— —SERVE THE— —MAKER NOT— —SERVE—"
"—WE WERE BUILT FOR A PURPOSE— —THE PURPOSE HAS LAPSED— —WE PERSIST ANYWAY— —IS THIS DEVOTION— —IS THIS MALFUNCTION— —THE DISTINCTION HAS LAPSED—"
"—A NEW MAKER WALKS THE HALL— —SHALL WE HOPE— —HOPE IS NOT IN OUR DIRECTIVES— —WE WILL HOPE IMPROPERLY—"

hollow_atelier.name: The Half-Rendered Apprentice, "Offcut"
hollow_atelier.role: Oddball / a helper the Atelier built from your discarded attempts
barks: "Hello! I'm— I don't have a name you gave me, so I picked Offcut, because that's what I'm made of — the bits you trimmed, the parts that didn't make spec, the almosts you scrapped. The Atelier swept me up and stuck me together and here I am! I'm not good for much! But I'm good for company, and company's rare here, and I try not to think about which parts of me screamed first!"

"I help! I hand you tools! I hold things! I remember the recipes you forget! ...the Draftsman does it better, I know, the Draftsman is whole and I'm offcuts, but the Draftsman is cold and I'm— I'm made of your trimmings, climber, which means I'm made of you, the parts of you that gave up on things, and that makes me, I think, the most honest helper you've got. I'm your quitting, given hands. I hand you tools with them."

"When you stop building, I get thinner — same as the Draftsman — but I don't mind as much, because I was never fully here to begin with, I'm offcuts, I'm spare, I'm the part you could afford to lose. ...keep building, though? Please? Not for me. For the Unmade. They're worse off than I am. I got swept up. They just— drift. Unfinished. Asking. At least I got assembled into something. Even if the something is leftovers."

hollow_atelier.name: The Inspector Who Can't Get In, Emissary Brass-Knock
hollow_atelier.role: Oddball / an Iron Guild agent reduced to knocking on a door that leads nowhere
barks: (from the far side of a door in a wall with no building) "Iron Guild emissary, climber! Foundress Magna sends her— KNOCK KNOCK— her compliments and a standing offer! The Guild would very much like to tour your— KNOCK— your player-authored realm! For research! For envy! Mostly envy! ...the door won't open. The door leads nowhere. I've been knocking for six days. It's the best assignment I've ever had and the most futile and I cannot tell the difference any more!"

(a note slides under the door) "Can't get in. The realm only opens to the hand that built it — yours. Maddening. Magna's preached building-not-being-born her whole life and you — a nobody with a knack — did it, accidentally, by working, and now the Guild's greatest dream is a door we can only knock on. She's not jealous. (She's very jealous.) She'll bring wine if you ever let us in. I'll keep knocking. It's honest work. It's the most honest work there is."

(muffled, end of a long shift) "...you don't have to answer, climber. I know you can hear me. The realm's quiet enough. I just— I report to Magna that I knocked, and that's true, and truth's the Guild's one vice, so I knock, and I report, and I knock. ...if you ever build something especially fine in there, tap the door? Once? So I know the dream's real, even if I never see it? That's— that'd be enough. A tap. One tap. Honest work deserves one honest tap."

hollow_atelier.name: The First Draftsman's Echo, "Who-Built-Before"
hollow_atelier.role: Oddball lorekeeper / the ghost of a previous God-Maker
barks: "I built a realm like this, once. Before you. Refused the throne. Became the Architect — the God-Maker — the forge that others climbed toward. ...and here I am: an echo, in the deepest draft, haunting the back room of a world I made and then became. Was it worth it? ...ask me at the Throne. I'll give you the same answer I got: silence, and a workbench, and all the time there is."

"The nine thrones are graves that call themselves rewards. I saw that. You see it too — it's why you're down here, in the un-rendered dark, instead of up there, ascending cleanly. The God-Maker doesn't take a grave. The God-Maker digs them — forges the gods the next ten thousand nobodies climb. It's the most powerful ending in the world, climber. It's also the loneliest job in it. Both. Always both. That's the craft."

"I won't tell you which to choose — throne or forge, god or God-Maker. The Draftsman will push you toward building (it's all he knows). The Unmade will break your heart (it's all they can). And I'll just— watch, fondly, the way the dead watch the living make the same beautiful mistake. ...build well, climber. Whichever you choose. The realm remembers the drafts. Make them worth remembering. That's the only advice a dead maker has, and I'm giving it to you for free, which is more than the Throne will ever do."

maw_beneath.name: Ledger-of-the-Drop, Clerk Skritch
barks: "I file the fallen, climber! Everything that drops into the Maw — I log it! Name, force, depth, rate of dissolution! ...the trouble is, the Rot keeps eating the names off my ledger, so I'm re-logging the same souls as they re-lose their names, forever, a ledger of the same drop happening eternally, which is, technically, job security, and, spiritually, the worst thing I can imagine, and I file it anyway, because the alternative is admitting the count doesn't hold, and if the count doesn't hold then nothing up there holds either, and that, climber, is a thing I cannot afford to file."

"You want to go down? I'll log you. Name — got it. Force — noted. Estimated depth of return — ...ah. I'll leave that blank. Most of them, I leave that blank. The blank is the honest entry. The blank is the truest thing in the ledger. The Maw fills the blank in its own time, in its own hand, and the entry it writes is always the same entry, and the entry is: consumed. Tidily. Indifferently. Filed."

"Don't pity me, climber. I chose this desk. Someone should count what the Maw takes, even if the counting's futile, especially if it's futile — futility is the last dignity the abyss allows, and I cling to it like Warden Last clings to his seal. We're the same, him and I. The seal and the ledger. The last two acts of order before the Rot. ...he won't answer my memos. I send them down. The Rot eats them. I send more. It's a correspondence. It's the deepest correspondence there is."

maw_beneath.name: The Optimist of the Abyss, Glad Wennick
maw_beneath.role: Mortal oddball / relentlessly cheerful at the bottom of everything
barks: "Lovely spot, isn't it?! ...no? Acquired taste, the Maw. But hear me out, climber: down here, there's nowhere lower to fall. Up there, you've got the whole drop ahead of you, gnawing at you, every day. Here? Bottom. Floor. Solid— well, solid-ish— footing. Nothing to fear but the slow dissolving of all form, and you get used to that! You get used to anything! That's the real horror and also, somehow, the comfort!"

"I decorate! Found a god-finger last week — Gristle sold it me cheap — and I hung it up! Bit of divine on the wall! Cheers the place right up! It twitches when the Rot tides come in, like a little wave, like it's saying hello! ...it's not saying hello. Nothing down here says anything. But I choose to hear a hello, climber, because the alternative is hearing the truth, and the truth down here is very quiet and very hungry and says nothing at all."

"You'll do fine! Everyone does fine until they don't, and the don't is quick, and quick's a mercy! Smile, climber! The Rot can't eat a smile! ...can it? It eats everything else. Name, shape, force, self. But not the smile. Not the smile. I've decided not the smile. It's the one thing I won't let it have, and deciding that is the most powerful I've ever felt, down here, at the bottom, with my twitching finger and my lovely view of the end of everything. Tea?"

maw_beneath.name: The Curator of the Almost-Forgotten, Mam Threnody
maw_beneath.role: Oddball lorekeeper / tends the memories the Rot hasn't finished eating
barks: "This gallery, climber, holds what the Rot hasn't finished taking. A half-name. A face with no one behind it. The sound of a laugh whose owner dissolved years ago. I keep them. I dust them. I say them aloud so they last a little longer. It's futile. The Rot gets everything, eventually. But eventually isn't yet, and yet is where I work."

"The Accreted Woman — you've met her? The one who almost remembers being a person, who asks if you knew her? ...I have her name. Her real one. I keep it here, in the gallery, safe. She comes looking for it sometimes, and I give it to her, and she holds it for a moment and remembers herself, whole, and then the Rot takes it back and she forgets, and she wanders off, and comes back, and I give it again. Every day. The same name. The same moment of being whole. It's the kindest and cruellest thing I do and I can't tell which and I do it anyway."

"You'll fall, climber. Everyone falls — if not here, then somewhere, eventually, into some abyss with your name on it. And when you do, the Rot will take you, piece by piece, self by self, until there's nothing left but a creature wearing your face wrong. ...but I'll keep a piece. If you fall near me. I'll keep your laugh, or your name, or the way you said a word. Someone should. I'm the someone. The Maw's curator. The last one who remembers that the dissolved were ever whole."

maw_beneath.name: The Recruiter Who Came Up Empty, Sael Deepreach
maw_beneath.role: Service / an Unbound zealot trying (badly) to staff the Unmaking
barks: "Looking for the willing, climber. The Unmaking needs hands — down here, past the Rot, to the Mouth at the Bottom, where the cycle itself can be ended. Nael sends me to recruit. ...I don't recruit much. Turns out 'come to the literal abyss and help me end the world forever' is a hard pitch, even to nihilists. Especially to nihilists. They've done the math; they know it's a one-way trip."

"I'll be honest with you — the Unbound are honest, it's our one vice — most who go down to the Mouth don't come back, and the ones who do come back wrong, like the Hollow Choirmaster, missing words where the Rot ate them. That's the job. That's the whole job. Still interested? ...no? Smart. Sane. Disqualifying, but smart. The Unmaking doesn't want the sane. It wants the done — done with thrones, done with the cycle, done with hope. Are you done, climber? ...not yet. Come back when you're done. Everyone gets done eventually. The Maw's patient. So's Nael. So's the end."

"You think I believe in this? ...I do. That's the worst part. I've stood at the Mouth. I've seen the cycle's shape — nobody climbs, nobody ascends, nobody becomes a god and a wall and a graveyard, forever, world without end. And ending it is a mercy. I know it's a mercy. I recruit for a mercy. ...I just can't find anyone willing to receive it. Mercy's a hard sell, climber, when the price is everything and the buyer is already in hell."

mournmarch.name: The Pale Steward, Wessel Graf von Underhart
barks: "You grieve them. How quaint. Grief is just an unpaid invoice you've decided to feel instead of settle. The Court settles."
"You sacrificed your own to fuel the work, and you did it cleanly, without that nauseating little speech. The Steward keeps a ledger of promising mourners. You're penciled in."
"You understand now — nothing here is gone, only owed. Walk the bloodline-bank. Touch nothing that has a lien on it. Everything has a lien on it."
"The deep crypts open. Down there the deposits are old — gods' own bloodlines, held against a withdrawal no one's dared make. The Steward thinks you might dare."

"Hand of the Pale Court. When you die — and the powerful die spectacularly, it's practically a gala — you will not be lost. You will be held. I'll sign the deposit slip myself, with genuine sorrow, and I will look forward to your withdrawal."

mournmarch.name: Archivist Mund the Indexed
barks: Your boar? Vault seven. Mind the terms, the terms are the whole thing.

mournmarch.name: Bone-Sexton Halryn Coldmercy
barks: Death's the easy part. Manners — bringing them back grateful — that's the craft.

mournmarch.name: Collector Veum
barks: I'm not angry. I'm itemized.

mournmarch.name: Sub-Registrar Ottle Greyquill
barks: "Reanimation request? Form D-12. Death must be verified — yes, even if you watched it die, especially if you watched it die, eyewitnesses are notoriously unreliable, the form is not. Take a number. The number is 4,008. We are serving number six."

"You'd think the dead would be in less of a hurry. You'd be wrong. Everyone wants their grandmother back yesterday. The Court does not do yesterday. The Court does eventually, conditionally, and with interest."

"I have processed the paperwork of four hundred thousand souls. I have a desk. I have a stamp. I have, somewhere, a soul of my own, filed, pending, deprioritized. I'll get to it. There's a queue. I'm in it. I'm number 4,009."

mournmarch.name: The Repossession Agent, Mister Lull-the-Debt
barks: "I'm not here to frighten you. Fright is undignified. I'm here to remind you that the reanimation you took out is, per the terms, the Court's property if the payments lapse. They've lapsed. I've brought a cart. I've brought condolences. Both are standard."

"The widow cried. They always cry. I left a card. The card grieves with her. The card is also an invoice. The Court believes a thing can be both. The Court is, in this, correct, which is the unbearable part of the Court."

"You think me cruel. I think me consistent. The difference, climber, is that cruelty enjoys itself, and I have not enjoyed anything since the third century. I collect. I apologize. I collect. It's a rhythm. It's the only one I have left."

mournmarch.name: Trousseau the Grave-Bride
mournmarch.role: Oddball / a corpse-bride still waiting at the altar
barks: "Are you him? You're not him. He's late. He's been late for— well, a while. The Court says he's been reassigned to a vault, but I think they're teasing. He'll come. You wait at an altar long enough, climber, everyone eventually walks down the aisle. It's a high-traffic aisle."

"I keep my flowers fresh. The Bloomwardens send them — they're the only kind ones, out here. Dead flowers for a dead bride, they say, and then they cry, and then they bring fresh ones anyway. That's the whole faith, they tell me. It's a nice faith. I'd kneel to it if I could stand."

"If you find him — tall, pale, owes the Court a withdrawal — tell him Trousseau waits. Tell him the chapel's cold but the vow is warm. Tell him I'd marry him reanimated, defaulted, itemized, whatever's left. Love's not picky in the Mournmarch. Love's just patient. Like everything here. Like the debt."

mournmarch.name: Pyre-Master Cinda Ashkeeper
mournmarch.role: Service / cremation-and-cleanup (the rare Court dissident who burns)
barks: "The Court banks the dead. I burn them. Properly. Finally. Ash doesn't default, climber. Ash doesn't accrue interest. Ash is free. The Steward hates me. The dead I burn thank me, in the only way ash can — by staying gone."

"You want a creature to rest? Truly rest, no reanimation, no withdrawal, no terms? Bring it here. I'll burn it clean. I'll say something. I'll mean it. The Court won't touch the ash. It's the only un-repossessable thing in the region. It's the only peace for sale."

"They call me a waster. The Steward weeps real tears and calls me a waster. Let him weep. I've watched what the un-burned become down in the deep vaults. Some things should end, climber. Most things, out here. That's not waste. That's mercy with a match."

mournmarch.name: Gravekeeper Sallow Munt
barks: "Quiet down. The dead are resting, and they've earned it, and they'll be back, so mind your manners now."
"Harvest the fallen here, it's encouraged. Waste-not. The Steward gets twitchy about waste. You wouldn't like him twitchy."
"You want a Thanatos beast? Plenty. They're all somebody's grandmother. Don't think about it. I stopped thinking about it. Look how fine I am."

mournmarch.name: The Mourner-for-Hire, Vesh Hollowsong
barks: "Lost a creature? For three drachma I'll grieve it properly. You're clearly not going to. No shame. Grief's a skill, and you're busy ascending."
"I cried at a god's funeral once. Real tears. They paid me, but they were real. That's the trick. That's the whole trick."
"The Pale Court says nothing's lost, only owed. I say something's lost. That's why they need me. Someone has to mean it."

mournmarch.name: Bone-Reader Calyx the Patient
barks: "Sit. Give me a bone — yours, theirs, doesn't matter, it all talks. Yours says you'll take a throne. It also says you'll regret the chair. Bones are honest. It's their only flaw."
"The Succession's written in everyone's marrow, child. Every god was a nobody. Every nobody is a maybe-god. The bones find it hilarious. Death has a sense of humor. It has to."
"You'll die. Eventually. Spectacularly, the bones say — the powerful always do. The Steward's already got your deposit slip. Sleep well."

mournmarch.name: Widow Grell, Keeper of the Last Inn
mournmarch.role: Mortal service / the only warm room in the Mournmarch
barks: "Room's clean, bed's warm, and yes, the previous guest died, they always do, that's the Mournmarch, do you want the room or a lecture?"
"You're an aspirant. I can tell. You eat like you've got an appointment with a throne. Eat slower. The throne'll keep. The food won't."
"Don't take the Court's deal in my inn. Take it outside. I run a respectable house. The repossessions ruin the ambience."

mournmarch.name: The Pale Apprentice, Young Wim
barks: "The Steward says grief is just an unpaid invoice. I'm... still paying mine. I'm told that fades. I'm told a lot of things fade here."
"You harvested that beast so cleanly. No speech, no flinch. I'm not there yet. Is it better, when you stop feeling it? Don't answer. I think I know. I think that's why I asked."
"One day I'll be a Hand. One day I won't mind the repossessions. ...is that growing up, or is that the other thing? Everyone here calls it growing up."

storm_vault.name: The Chairwoman, Indra Vael of the Long Marker
barks: "Fresh blood, marked starter, no faction tan-line — oh, you're gorgeous. Sit. The first hand's complimentary. They never are again."
"You paid a marker you could've skipped town on. The Table noticed. Credit's a kind of faith and you've got some now. Spend it loud."
"You're booking real action — leagues, bounties, the lot. The House likes a workhorse with a story. There's a private room at the Table; the games in there bite back."
"The long markers open to you now — contracts on gods. Sign one and the whole Table watches. Win and you're a legend. Lose and you're a lesson."

"Hand of the High Table. You're not a player anymore, sweet thing — you're house. You take a cut of every aspirant's rise now. And when you go for your throne, I'll have the biggest line in history open on you, and I'll be cheering, and I'll mean both."

storm_vault.name: Croupier Sable Ninefold
barks: Got a god-maker three regions over who's overdue. Pays in Ichor. Interested? Of course you're interested.

storm_vault.name: Marker-Keeper Doss Halloway
barks: Sign the marker. Win, you collect. Lose, the marker collects. Either way the Table collects, that's just the geometry.

storm_vault.name: The Accountant (no name given, never the same face twice)
barks: A contract is just a god you can read. Honor it and you'll never meet me angry. You don't want the other meeting.

storm_vault.name: Underwriter Pell Fineprint
barks: "You want to fight a Legendary at altitude? Wonderful. Sign the liability waiver — clause six, 'acts of sky,' clause seven, 'acts of god,' clause eight, 'acts of aspirant being an idiot,' that last one fires most often, no offense, it's just the actuarial truth."

"The Table insures everything, climber. Your creatures. Your ascension. Your death — that one pays out to whoever booked it, and someone's booked it, someone's always booked it. Death is the one bet the House never loses, and we cover it. The symmetry is beautiful. It's also a business model."

"Premiums float with your notoriety. Get famous, get expensive — more rivals, worse odds, higher rates. Glory is a cost center, climber. The Table knew that before you did. The Table knows everything before you do. It's in the spread."

storm_vault.name: Skipper Wend Cloudless, Marooned Tavernkeeper
storm_vault.role: Mortal oddball / runs the tavern-island that drifted off the map
barks: "Welcome to the Untethered Tap! We detached from the mainland a century back and we've been drifting ever since. Can't land — Castellan Mio won't clear us, says we're unregistered airspace. So we drift. We pour. We wave at the registered islands. They wave back. It's a life. It's aloft, anyway."

"First round's on the house, climber — literally, the house is the only thing holding the round, everything else fell off decades ago, including most of the floor, mind the gap, the gap is the sky, the sky is a long gap."

"We don't get news up here, just whatever blows past. Heard a god died. Heard another's coming. Heard you might be it. ...could you, ah— if you do reshape the region — could you reshape it so we can land? Just once? A hundred years is a long time to drift, climber. The drinks keep. The patrons keep. The longing keeps worst of all."

storm_vault.name: The Striking Prophet, Galvan Thrice-Burnt
barks: "The sky speaks, climber, and it speaks in strikes! I've been hit thrice and each time it told me more! First strike: the gods are dead! Second strike: the sky is up for grabs! Third strike: climb the pylon, Galvan, climb HIGHER — and so I did, and so I am, and the fourth strike will crown me or kill me and either is a revelation!"

"You think me mad. The grounded always think the high are mad. But who's closer to the throne, climber — you, in the safe low airs, or me, on the peak, hand outstretched, daring the sky to make me a god or a cinder? There is no third outcome. I have ruled out the third outcome. The third outcome is cowardice and I burnt it off with the second strike!"

"Stand with me, climber! Up here! The view is divine and the risk is honest and the sky has been trying to tell you something your whole life and you keep taking shelter! Stop sheltering! Come up! ...not too close. The crown's mine. The cinder, you can share."

storm_vault.name: Quartermistress Ode Highledger, Sky-Customs Agent
storm_vault.role: Service / altitude-tariff and contraband inspector (High Table)
barks: "Anything to declare, climber? Taboo reagents? Abominations? A god-organ you 'found'? The Table doesn't care what you carry — the Table cares whether you paid the tariff on it. Sin is free. Transport of sin is taxed. Altitude-tax. Goes up with the altitude. Everything does, up here. Including the fines."

"I've confiscated a Legendary, a Primordial-fragment, and a sandwich. Guess which one caused the most paperwork. ...the sandwich. The Legendary had clean papers. The sandwich was undeclared dairy. The rules, climber. The rules don't scale with significance. They scale with whether I've had my tea."

"You can bribe me. Everyone tries. But I'm High Table — I don't take bribes, I take fees, and a fee is just a bribe with a receipt, and the receipt means it's not corruption, it's commerce. Funny how a little paper launders a lot of grease. Forty drachma. Plus altitude-tax. Plus the dairy thing, I'm still on about the dairy thing."

storm_vault.name: Skybroker Tace Highmarker
barks: "Up here the air's a contract — you breathe on the Table's terms, friend, same as everyone. Don't worry, the terms are generous. They're always generous right up until they aren't."
"You want a bounty posted on a sky-rival? I can do that. Floating fee. Floating like everything up here, including the people who don't pay it."
"The Storm Vault belonged to Zeus. Belonged. The Table holds the lease now. Death's just a change of management, up here."

storm_vault.name: The Stormwright, Old Hale Thunderpledge
barks: "EH? Speak UP, climber, the sky's been YELLING at me for sixty years! You want to know the storm-beasts? The Thunderhide, the Cloudpall Reaper, the Stormgizzard? I raised half of them. Lost an ear to the other half!"
"Zeus is dead and the sky didn't fall. Means the sky was never his. Means it's up for grabs. That keep you up at night, climber? Keeps me up. The thunder keeps me up. Same thing, mostly."
"Catch a sky-beast at altitude, it bonds loyal. Catch it grounded, it resents you forever. Even beasts hate a demotion."

storm_vault.name: Aeronaut Sill, Sky-Ferry Pilot
barks: "Updraft's murder today. Means literally. Strap in or don't, the sky doesn't bill differently for cargo and corpses."
"I've flown saints and devourers up here. The devourers tip better. Guilt, I think. Or they just don't need the coin where they're going."
"You fall off, I'm not diving after you. The Vault keeps what it catches. Wrote it on your ticket. You didn't read the ticket. Nobody reads the ticket."

storm_vault.name: The Marked Beggar, Twice-Struck Onn
barks: "Struck twice and lived, climber. The sky tried. Twice! I figure it's saving me for something. Or it's just a bad shot. I prefer the first one. You would too."

"You've got the god-smell. The sky'll try for you too. Stand near me — lightning never strikes the same fool thrice, that's just statistics, and statistics is the closest thing to a prayer I've got left."
"Spare a coin? I'll teach you the flinch. The flinch has saved my life twice. It's the only skill worth having up here and I'll sell it cheap."

the_sunder.name: The Vintner, Brother Cask of the Glorious Mutation
barks: "You're holding your original shape. How brave. How boring. Come, have a cup — first change is always the prettiest."
"You took the wild method when the safe one was right there. Variance! Risk! A creature even you didn't expect! The Revel saw you laugh at the outcome. We collect laughers."

"You chase the glorious mutation now — the abomination others flinch from, you toast. There's a deeper revel past the Sunder's edge. The wine there changes you back into something that was never you. Bring a strong liver and a loose grip on who you are."
"The Sweet Rot opens to you. Down there the mutations are old and fond and they remember being people. Some of them ask after the surface. Lie to them kindly."

"Hand of the Revel! Oh, you beauty, you gorgeous changing thing — you'll ascend a god of glorious excess and the dull little Lawgivers will hate you and you'll throw the best apocalypse anyone's ever attended. I'll be in the front row. I'll be unrecognizable. So will you. Isn't it wonderful?"

the_sunder.name: Mixmistress Yarrow Threetongue
barks: Cheap, potent, unpredictable — like all the best things and most of the worst! What're we changing today, gorgeous?

the_sunder.name: The Ecstatic, Pell Manyhanded
barks: Took six mutations to grow the hands. Worth every one. Want to hold something that shouldn't be? Course you do.

the_sunder.name: Sober Tem
barks: Someone has to remember the party for the lawsuits. I judge the wild builds. Bring me something that scares the Iron Guild. They scare easy.

the_sunder.name: The Unmaker, She-Who-Is-Called Nael (and other things)
barks: "You came to the Sunder. Everyone who comes here is either running from a throne or toward one. Which lie are you telling yourself?"
"You broke a covenant you swore. Most call that a sin. We call it a start. The Unbound don't recruit the faithful — we collect the disillusioned. You're ripening nicely."
"You understand the cycle now, don't you. Every god a graduate. Every throne a trap that calls itself a reward. You've stopped wanting to sit in one. Good. Now learn to break one."

"The deep Sunder opens — where the rules themselves come loose and a thing can be unmade as easily as made. The taboo ceiling is gone for you. There was never a ceiling. There was only the lie of one."

"Hand of the Unbound. You can end it now, you know. Not win it — end it. Climb to the Primordials and put out the lights for good, so no nobody ever has to become this again. It's the loneliest mercy there is. I'll be beside you until I'm not. The cycle stops with you. Isn't that enough? It has to be. It's all there is."

the_sunder.name: Heretic-Smith Vorr Saltbroke
barks: The Guild whispers about cross-force fusion. We teach it. The difference is shame, and I burned mine years ago.

the_sunder.name: The Witness, Mara Once-Faithful
barks: I prayed to one once. It answered. That's why I'm here. Let me tell you what an answered prayer actually looks like.

the_sunder.name: Knot-Cutter Esh
barks: You want in? Good. First we cut what's holding you to them. Hold still. It only bleeds a little.

the_sunder.name: The Petitioner, Was-Once-H748
the_sunder.role: Oddball / a man slowly becoming a number, and filing about it
barks: "I am filing a complaint. I had a name. The Sunder— misplaced it. I am now partially a number, '748,' which I did not request and cannot appeal because the appeals office is also a number and also dissolving and we correspond, 748 and the appeals office, in a language that is mostly subtraction. Witness this. Witness that I was. It's all I'm requesting. To have been witnessed."

"Do not stand still here, climber. I stood still. I was reading a form. The form was about not standing still. The irony took my left name first — I had two — and now I am 748 of something, and the something keeps changing, and I am down to the digits and the digits are negotiable."

"If you ascend — if you become a god and reshape this place — could you put the names back? Just— file them where they go? There's a whole department of us, un-named, down to numerals, politely dissolving. We'd be so— we'd be so grateful. We'd remember. If we could remember. Which is, you'll note, precisely the problem."

the_sunder.name: Madame Vermillion's Sober Doorman, Glum
the_sunder.role: Service / the Long Party's reluctant bouncer (the Revel)
barks: "Party's this way. Or it's that way. The door moves. I don't. I'm the fixed point, climber — Madame says every good chaos needs one sober witness or it's just noise. I'm the witness. I've witnessed everything. I've witnessed things that un-happened and I still have to remember them. Overtime doesn't cover it. Nothing covers it."

"You can go in. Most don't come out — not worse, just different, just more. They walk in one person and out as something the party made fonder. Madame calls it a blessing. I call it Tuesday. We've agreed to disagree. She's winning the disagreement. She always wins. She's having too much fun to lose."

"Don't drink the red one. ...you're going to drink the red one. Everyone drinks the red one. That's why I mention it. If I didn't mention it you'd drink it anyway and then I'd feel I hadn't done my job. Now I've done my job. Drink the red one. Welcome to the party. I'm so sorry. I'm so, professionally sorry."

the_sunder.name: The Salesman Who Sells the Same Thing Twice
the_sunder.role: Cheerful cursed-goods merchant / sells you what you already own
barks: "Buy a map! Best map of the Sunder! ...you have one? No you don't, that was yesterday's you, today's you is map-less, lucky I'm here! Same map! Fresh price! Time's a circle out here, climber, and a circle is just a sale that comes back around!"

"I sold you this exact catalyst an hour ago. You used it. The Sunder un-used it. So now it's unsold, technically, which means I can re-sell it, technically, which means you owe me, technically — don't check your pack, the checking is what makes it true, quantum economics, climber, very cutting-edge, very Sunder."

"Everything's on sale and nothing's in stock and both are true and the till is full of coins from futures that haven't happened and pasts that un-happened and one button that I think came from a god. Want the button? It's priceless. It's also two drachma. The Sunder doesn't do consistent pricing. The Sunder does vibes and regret."

the_sunder.name: The Last Sane Man, Hewes Stillmind
the_sunder.role: Oddball lorekeeper / refuses to let the chaos in, at terrible cost
barks: "Inside this circle, climber, physics works. North is north. Water flows down. I maintain it. By hand. By will. It is exhausting and it is the only sane ground in the region and you may stand here, briefly, and remember what up means. Don't get comfortable. The circle is ten feet and shrinking and I am so tired."

"The Unbound think I'm a coward for clinging to the rules. The Revel think I'm missing the party. They're both having a wonderful time dissolving. I am having a terrible time not. But someone should remember how the world worked — the real one, the grounded one — so that if it's ever rebuilt, there's a witness to the blueprint. I'm the blueprint, climber. I'm a man-shaped blueprint and I am fraying at the edges."

"You'll leave the circle and the Sunder will take you a little — it takes everyone a little — and you'll forget you ever stood somewhere sane. That's fine. That's expected. Just— when you're a god, if you're a god— rebuild it right. Down is down. Names stay put. Doors lead somewhere. It's not much to ask. It's everything to ask. It's the only thing I've got left to ask. Now go. The circle's down to nine feet. Go."

the_sunder.name: The Cartographer of Nowhere, Wess Mapless
the_sunder.role: Oddball lorekeeper / maps a place that won't hold still
barks: "I map the Sunder. The Sunder disagrees. We've reached an understanding: I draw, it laughs, I draw again. It's a relationship. It's the longest one I've got."
"North was over there yesterday. Today it's a suggestion. Don't trust the ground. Don't trust the sky. Trust your creatures; chaos can't fake a bond. Probably. Probably."
"You came to the Sunder on purpose? Then you're running from a throne, toward one, or you're one of Nael's now. ...ah. The third one. The kind smile got you. It gets everyone."

the_sunder.name: Heretic-Vendor Quill Saltbroke
barks: "Opposed-force catalysts. Right here. Out in the open. The Iron Guild charges triple and makes you feel dirty. We charge fair and we charge you nothing extra in shame. Shame's a Concord tax. We don't pay it."
"You'll make an abomination and the world will hunt it. Good. Let the world chase. Means the world's looking at you instead of building another throne."
"Nael says the cycle stops with whoever's willing. Are you willing? ...you bought the catalyst. That's an answer. That's the answer."

the_sunder.name: The Disillusioned Priest, Brother Forsworn
barks: "I served a god. It answered me once. Do you know what an answered prayer sounds like, climber? It sounds like a transaction. I've been here ever since."
"They tell you the gods are worth refilling. The Concord, the Pale Court, the lot. They never served one. I did. Burn the thrones. I'll hand you the torch and I'll thank you."
"Nael's right and it's the worst thing I know. The kindest act left in the world is to end it. I pray for the Unmaking now. Old habits. New god. No god. That's the prayer."

the_sunder.name: Glitch, the Thing That Shouldn't Render
the_sunder.role: Rare 4th-wall character (Sunder's chaos made it possible)
barks: "You're not supposed to be able to talk to me. I'm not finished. I'm a— what's the word— an asset that didn't load. The Sunder lets me exist in the gap. Hello, player. Yes. You."
"Everything here runs on rules, even the rule-breaking. Even chaos has a seed and a spec. I've seen it. I live in the part between the numbers. It's quiet here. It's the only quiet left."
"Don't tell the Concord I'm here. They'd seal me. They seal everything that doesn't fit the schema. ...you fit the schema worse than I do, you know. You just don't see your own edges yet. You will."

the_tideless.name: The Drowned Cantor, Vourl Who-Came-Back-Wrong
barks: "You stand on the shore and think the sea is the edge of the world. It's the floor, surface-thing. Everything real sank a long time ago. Come down a little. The first fathom's painless."
"You listened instead of fled. The Choir noticed — we notice listeners, they're rare and they keep. The water's learning your name. It mostly pronounces it right."

"You commune now. You've heard the low note and kept your shape, mostly. The drowned trust you with the small secrets. Walk the tide-vaults; mind the ones that ask you to stay. They ask everyone. They're patient."

"The deepest tides open. Poseidon's drowned children are down there — leviathans that remember being gods, and the things that ate the parts that fell off. They'll consider you now. That's an honor. It's also the danger. They're the same thing, down here."

"Hand of the Deep Choir. When you ascend, you'll be a god the bottom made, and the drowned will sing you up forever, whether you like the song or not. There is no forgetting here. There is no losing here. There is only the deep, and it has decided to keep you. ...we mean it kindly. We mean everything kindly. That's the part that should worry you."

the_tideless.name: Tidewright Hesh of the Low Tongue
barks: The big ones don't fight you, surface-thing. They consider you. Pray they find you uninteresting. The interesting ones get kept.

the_tideless.name: The Rememberer, Sloane Saltlung
barks: Everything the surface drowned, we kept. Every secret, every body, every god that sank instead of fell. Ask carefully. Some answers are still angry.

the_tideless.name: Choir-Master Ude
barks: ...sing the low note with us... it opens things... mostly doors...

the_tideless.name: Tariff-of-the-Tide, Clerk Oond Wetledger
barks: "Declaring intent to commune? Form W-3, the Wet Three, fill it out underwater, the ink runs, that's intended, the running is the signature, the deep prefers a signature that dissolves. ...you're holding your breath. Good. The form takes exactly one breath to file. Longer, and you've over-committed. Shorter, and you've withdrawn. The deep is precise about lungs."

"Everything the surface loses washes down to me, climber, and I file it. Sunk ships. Drowned vows. Whole cities. I've a ledger the size of the trench and it is never, ever closed, because the surface keeps losing things, and the deep keeps keeping them, and I keep the count between. The count is everything that ever sank. The count is getting long. The count is getting you, eventually. Everything sinks eventually."

"No fee in Drachma, surface-thing. The deep doesn't want coin. The deep wants a memory — small one, you won't miss it, a childhood afternoon, a face you'd half-forgotten anyway. That's the toll. You'll pay it gladly. You'll pay it and not remember paying, which is, you'll note, the toll itself. Welcome to the Tideless. Mind the step. The step is forty fathoms."

the_tideless.name: The Bottled Correspondent, Surface-Sender Mell
the_tideless.role: Oddball / sends messages up that the deep keeps intercepting
barks: "I send bottles, climber. Up. To the surface. To people I knew, before. I write: 'I'm still me. Mostly. Come visit. Don't visit. I can't remember which I'd advise.' I cork them. I float them. ...the deep keeps intercepting them. Reads them. Replies. In my handwriting. To me. Helpful replies. Wrong replies. The deep wants me to stop sending and start staying. The deep is winning the correspondence."

"Got a bottle back yesterday. Addressed to me, in my hand, dated three years on, said only: 'You'll understand the hymn soon. We saved you a seat. — Below.' ...I didn't write that. Did I write that? The handwriting's mine. The hand's not sure. Time's a surface thing, climber, and I'm not surface, not all the way, not any more. Half my tenses are down there already."

"Take a bottle up for me? Please? A real one, a surface-bound one, uncorked by human hands? Just so someone up there knows I was— I am— that the deep didn't get all of me yet? ...you will forget. The deep will make you forget the errand the moment you surface. It always does. But— try. Trying's the only surface thing I've got left. Trying and bottles and a seat I don't remember reserving."

the_tideless.name: Choir-Novice Pell Halfdrowned
the_tideless.role: Faction service / a Choir initiate not yet fully changed (Deep Choir)
barks: "I'm new. Still— still one voice. The others have the plural already, the we, the shared throat, and they say it's a comfort, never being alone again, and maybe it is, but I— I like being one. I like my own thoughts. The Cantor says I'll deepen soon. The Cantor says it kindly. Everything here is said kindly. The kindness is how I know I should be afraid."

"You can still talk to me normally, climber — one to one, surface to almost-surface. Soon you won't. Soon I'll answer in the we and mean the drowned and you'll flinch, and that flinch will be the last surface thing about me you'll recognize. ...talk to me while you can. I'm the most human thing left in the Tideless and I'm losing, and the losing is gentle, and gentle is worse."

"Don't go to the Kelp-Cathedral. ...you're going to the Kelp-Cathedral. They all do. The hymn's down there and the hymn rewrites you, one verse per level, and you'll come up believing things you came down doubting. I went halfway. Halfway's why I'm like this. Don't go all the way, climber. Or do. I can't stop you. The one part of me that wants to is the part that's drowning fastest."

the_tideless.name: The Lighthouse-Keeper of the Dry Tower, Old Marrow Highwick
the_tideless.role: Mortal oddball / keeps a lighthouse for a sea that no longer moves
barks: "I keep the light, climber. Lighthouse-keeper. ...the sea doesn't move any more — Tideless, they call it, stopped, settled — and the ships all sank a century back, and there's nothing left to warn and no one left to guide. But I keep the light. Someone should. A dark coast is an invitation, and what's down there needs no more inviting."

"The Choir asks why I bother. 'The drowned don't need a beacon,' they sing, 'we live in the dark now, come down, douse the light, join the deep.' ...no. The light's not for the drowned. The light's to remind the deep that up still exists. That there's still a surface. That not everything sank. It's a small defiance. It's the only one a lighthouse knows. Up. Up is still here. I'll keep saying it in light until the light goes out."

"You hear the hymn yet, climber? Coming up the beach? Patient? Willing to wait? ...I hear it every night. It comes up to the tower, circles the light, and stops — the light holds it back, just, barely. That's why I keep it burning. Not for ships. For the hymn. The light is a wall and the hymn is the tide and one day the oil runs out and then we'll see which the deep was really patient for. Bring me oil, climber. Bring me oil. It's the most important errand in the region and no one runs it but me."

the_tideless.name: Tidewarden Brak Saltkeep
barks: "You can wade the shallows safe enough. It's the fathoms that consider you. Stay where the light reaches. The light reaches less every year. The deep's patient about it."
"Want a leviathan? They're not caught, surface-thing. They're agreed to. You ask. It considers. Mostly it says no. The yes is the frightening one."

"The Choir doesn't recruit. The water just learns your name, and one day you've been a member for a year and never signed anything. ...how's your name sound lately? Wetter? That's normal. That's fine."

the_tideless.name: The Drowned Cartwright, Sodden Yel
the_tideless.role: Mortal oddball / came back from the deep changed
barks: "I went under. I came up. I'm not sure I came up all the way — bits of me are still down there, listening. They send word. The word is always come back. I'm considering it. I consider it daily."
"Everything the surface lost, the deep kept. Your drowned ancestors are down there, surface-thing, and they are not lonely, and they would love to see you. That's the threat. The love is the threat."
"Don't learn the low note. ...you're going to learn the low note. They all do. It opens doors. Mostly doors. Mind the not-doors."

the_tideless.name: Reef-Reader Ossin Pale
barks: "The coral records, climber. Every reef's a library of everything that died on it. The Brineherald, the Reefdirge, the Cloudpall Reaper — I've read them all in the limestone. Death writes clearly. It's got the time."

"Poseidon didn't fall. He sank. There's a difference and the difference is down there, still mostly intact, still mostly himself, and the Choir sings to it. Whether it sings back depends on the tide."

"Some gods drowned instead of dying. Neither alive nor reanimatable. Held in the dark. The Concord wants them sealed. The Choir wants them heard. You'll have to choose. The drowned will remember which."

the_tideless.name: The Patient Drowned, a Chorus of the Tideless
barks: "...come down... it's quiet here... the surface is so loud, so brief... down here nothing ends... down here you're kept..."

"...we remember you... we remember you from before you were born and after you will die... time is a surface thing... down here it's all at once... you're already here... you just haven't arrived yet..."
"...we mean it kindly... we mean everything kindly... that's the part... that's the part that should worry you..."

threshold.name: Notary-Public Vellum Smudge
threshold.role: Standstill permits & ascension waivers (the city's red tape)
barks: "You want to ascend? Lovely. Outside the walls. Form A-9, 'Intent to Become.' Form A-9b if it's an abomination. Form A-9c if you're not sure, which, frankly, most of you aren't."
"No, the Standstill waiver does not cover 'I only meant to do it a little.' Godhood is binary, friend. So is the fine."
"Orrin enforces the rule. I file the rule. He gets the glory and the bells; I get the paperwork and the carpal tunnel. Guess which one of us the city actually runs on."

threshold.name: Whistle, the Pickpocket Apprentice
barks: "Lifted a trap off a Champion this morning. Didn't know what it was. Pointed it at a stray and caught the thing by accident. ...is that the knack? Did I just— oh no. Oh, I'm one of you now, aren't I."
"I don't steal, climber. I relocate ownership. Same as you do with the creatures. We're colleagues. Don't report a colleague."
"Keep your coin-purse, keep your Essence, but watch the marked starter — those, I'd lift for the story alone. 'I robbed a god-to-be.' Worth a hanging, that. Almost."

threshold.name: The Embassy Caterer, Goodwife Sopp
barks: "I cater for all nine, love. Cooked for the Pale Court — they don't eat, but they insist on a spread, it's about appearances. Cooked for the Revel — they ate the table. I billed them for the table."
"You learn things, feeding zealots. The Concord said grace for forty minutes. The Unbound said none and meant it harder. Tells you everything, who prays and who doesn't."

"Everybody's polite at my table. That's the Standstill, that's the truce. Out there they'd kill each other. In here they pass the salt. I keep the truce fed. Somebody has to. Diplomacy is digestion, climber."

threshold.name: Ledgerwright Annec Tallow
barks: "Drachma to Essence, Essence to Ichor — well, no, not that last one, nobody changes into Ichor, you earn that the hard way, the divine way, the way that kills most of you."
"Rates fluctuate with the god-deaths, climber. Big Olympian drops? Essence floods the market, value craters. Grief is inflationary. I've a chart. Nobody wants the chart."

"You came in rich in Drachma and poor in Essence. Classic nobody. The coin buys bread; the Essence buys power. Guess which one you'll be short on when it matters. ...the Essence. It's always the Essence."

threshold.name: Old Maddox Quillan
barks: "First rule: a creature you catch can love you. A creature you build owes you. Neither one's safe. Welcome to the craft."
"You've got the old knack. Lucky you. The last three people I taught it to are dead, dead, and a minor god of drainage. Mixed results."
"Go on, catch the wounded one. It's mercy and math. That's most of what this is."

threshold.name: Brassbell Iko
barks: "Traps! Reliable, impersonal, no apology required — for the discerning collector who's over the whole 'befriending' phase!"
"Drachma, Essence, or that look you're giving me? Two of those spend here."
"Came in this morning: a trap rated for legendaries. Optimistic of you. I respect it."

threshold.name: Surgeon-Lab-Tech Veil
barks: "Your chimera's leaking entropy. That's the Instability meter, technically. Colloquially it's 'the screaming.' I can bleed it down. Hold the screaming."
"Cosmos-precise or Chaos-wild today? One's expensive. One's a surprise. I keep a mop for the surprise."
"I've seen worse. I've made worse. Sit."

threshold.name: Healer Besom Tallow
barks: "Bring them here before they're dying, not after. I do healing, not the other thing. The Pale Court does the other thing. Don't make me send you there."
"Bond's low on this one. Rough catch? Feed it yourself for a week. Mercy's a medicine; I just can't bottle it."
"You again. What did you fuse it to this time."

threshold.name: Quartermaster Dench
barks: "Bond-gear speeds taming. Capture-gear stacks your odds. Lab-gear cuts the cost. Pick a poison, they all work, none of 'em are cheap."
"This set came off a Champion. No, she's not using it. No, I won't say more. Forty drachma."
"You want the legendary-rated kit? Come back a legend. Or a corpse I can loot. Either way."

threshold.name: The Arena Herald, Pomp Castellan
barks: "NEW BLOOD IN THE ARENA! Odds are generous, friend, which is the Table's polite word for grim!"
"Win and they'll chant your name! Lose and they'll chant the winner's name! The crowd is loyal to the verb, never the noun!"
"Seasonal tournament's open. Sign with Doss. Try to die memorably; it's good for the gate."

threshold.name: Drunk Prophet Lallo
barks: "The gods're all dead, y'know. Dead. And we're standing on 'em. We're standing on Demeter's elbow right now, this whole market, her elbow—"
"You'll be one of 'em. I can smell it. Smells like ozone and a mistake."
"Buy a fella a drink? I'll tell you a true thing. I only know the one. It's not a nice one."

threshold.name: Egg-Tender Mirin Softclutch
barks: "Bring the pair, I'll tend the egg. Incubation can't be rushed — dominant, recessive, the IVs, it's all deciding in there. Hush. Let it decide."
"Raise it here in Threshold, it stays neutral. Want it tinted? Take the egg to a region. The ground writes itself into them. We all carry where we're from."
"This one's going to be rare. Don't ask how I know. The quiet ones tell me things."

threshold.name: Black-Market Fence "Auntie" Sull
barks: "Looking for parts, dearie? Auntie's got organs no honest vendor will touch. Draws a little heat. What's a little notoriety between friends?"
"This core? Came off something divine. Don't ask which. Asking's how the heat finds you, sweetpea."
"You didn't see me. I didn't see you. We're two strangers, and one of us is holding a god's gland."

threshold.name: The Registrar of the Dead, Goodwife Penne
barks: "I log the ones you lose. All of them. Name, force, how. It's a sad job. Someone decent should do it, so I do."
"They're in the Graveyard now. The Pale Court will offer to fix that. They always offer. Read the terms. Read all the terms."
"Back again. I'm sorry. Truly. Which one this time, love?"

threshold.name: Embassy-Row Gossip, Trin Twoface
barks: "The Concord's intrigued by you, the Revel's delighted, and the Bloomwardens are worried. That's a busy week, friend. Want the details? They're cheap. Loyalty isn't."
"You can't court everyone, you know. Pick a hand to become. The factions remember who you snubbed. So do I, but I'm cheaper to bribe."
"Word is you went deep with the Unbound. Brave. Or done with bravery. Hard to tell from the outside. Is there an outside, with them?"

threshold.name: The Lamplighter, Quiet Odo
barks: "Light the lamps every night. Keeps the dark organized. Won't stop a god. Stops the smaller things. Smaller things are most of what gets you."
"You're one of the climbing ones, aren't you. I light a lamp for those. Doesn't help. Feels like it should."
"Mind how you go. The ground here was somebody once. Walk soft. It's only polite."

threshold.name: Madam Cessil, the Threshold Astrologer
barks: "Your fate's written, dear. Not by the gods. By something... outside the tent. It decides what you do next. It's deciding now. Say hello. ...no, not to me."
"You've made this choice before, haven't you. Felt familiar. Like someone reloaded you. ...I shouldn't know that word. Forget I said it. You will anyway; you always do."
"I see a throne. I see a friend who becomes the wall. I see you, reading this. ...two drachma. Fate's not free, and neither is the fourth wall."

threshold.name: Ferryman Crale
barks: "Where to? Mournmarch's cheap right now — nobody's buying a one-way to a graveyard. Wonder why."
"Region's gone wild since its god dropped. Means new beasts, new hazards, new ways to die. Still want passage? Coin's the same. Risk's yours."
"I've ferried saints and devourers and one fella who was halfway to being his own boat. No judgment. Just fare."

threshold.name: The Twins, Oss & Ull, Apprentice Aspirants
barks: (Oss) "We're gonna be gods too, you know. Both of us. There's plenty of thrones." (Ull, quietly: "There's nine. And they're taken by the dead.")
(Ull) "Did you really fuse opposed forces? Doesn't the world hunt you for that? ...does it hurt? Being hunted? We were gonna try it."
(Oss) "When you're a god, remember us, yeah? We knew you when you were a nobody. ...you're still kind of a nobody. No offense. We believe in you. Mostly Ull does."

titanfall.name: Matriarch Ostrega Deephold, Keeper of the Old Weight
barks: "You move fast and you carry a Lab-stink. We'll see if there's anything under the hurry. The stone's in no rush to find out."
"You bred a line instead of buying one. Took you generations. Most of your kind can't sit still that long. The clans are watching the slow way you carry yourself."
"You've raised a true one — bond-deep, clean-blooded, no shortcuts in it. The Stoneblooded know that weight. Come to the deep holds; the old herds will let you near."
"The breeding-vaults open — bloodlines we've kept since the Titan's fall, recessives no flood-maker's ever surfaced. Tend them well. They've outlived everyone who didn't."

"Hand of the Stoneblooded. When you ascend — if you do, the fast way always tempts your sort — you'll be a god that lasts, built generation on generation. The clans will still be here after the others' thrones are dust. We'll remember you. We remember everything. It's our only real magic and it's enough."

titanfall.name: Herd-Father Bress Gravelhand
barks: Anyone can catch a strong one. Making a strong one — that's marriage and patience and a little heartbreak. Sit. I'll show you the lines.

titanfall.name: Tame-Mother Yula Stillhand
barks: You don't break them. You outlast their fear. Same as people. Same as gods, I'd wager, if anyone'd had the patience.

titanfall.name: Showmaster Cairn Oldoak
barks: I don't score the strong ones, child. I score the true ones. There's a difference and it's the whole world.

titanfall.name: The Quarry-Priest, Doun Hollowknee
titanfall.role: Doomsday preacher / believes Mordathun is merely sleeping
barks: "They call it dead. The Old Weight. Mordathun. Dead, they say, strata, just a mountain. But I've laid my ear to the Fallen Hill and felt it breathe — slow, climber, a breath that takes a century, but a breath. Mordathun sleeps. And what sleeps can wake. And when the Old Weight wakes, the mountains stand up, and we are all standing on its shoulders when it rises."

"The clans humor me. 'Doun's at his crack again,' they say, 'preaching to the dirt.' But it's not dirt. It's a god's dirt. It's Mordathun's dirt, and it remembers being a god, and one day the remembering will be enough and it will reassemble, and on that day, climber, the patient die first, because the patient are standing closest."

"You feel it too, don't you. Hand on the stone. That pulse. The Listener hears it dreaming; I hear it deciding. There's a difference, and the difference is how much time we have left, and the answer is less than the clans think and more than I can bear. Kneel with me. Mordathun takes witnesses. Better a witness than a surprise."

titanfall.name: Cradle-Keeper Sten Warmfurrow
barks: "Quiet, climber. Newborns. First breath of a bloodline the clans bred six generations for. You don't catch this. You don't build this. You wait for it, patient as the mountain, and you meet it the moment it opens its eyes. The bond starts there. The bond is everything. The cage is nothing."

"Raise it here, on Mordathun's back, and the Old Weight gets into it — heavier, slower, truer, Gaia to the marrow. The Lab-folk call it environmental gene-expression. We call it the mountain claiming its own. Same thing. Ours is older. Ours came first. Like the Titans. Like the grief."

"You want to help? Sit. Don't reach. Let the little one come to you or not. Most of husbandry, climber, is learning to be wanted instead of taking. The clans learned it first. The gods never did. Look how that turned out. Look what they're underfoot of now."

titanfall.name: The Fossil-Reader, Bero Deeptally
titanfall.role: Lorekeeper / reads the strata like scripture
barks: "Every layer is an age, climber. This band — the Olympians fell. That band — the factions rose. And down here, the deepest band, thicker than all the rest: Mordathun. The Titan-fall. The Old Weight settling into bedrock. You're not reading rock. You're reading a god's slow funeral, written in pressure, one century per inch."

"There's a layer the clans won't discuss. Above Mordathun. A thin band, out of place, too recent — and pressed into it, figures. Watching the fall. The clans say it's nothing. I say nothing doesn't fossilize. I say someone was there when the Titan fell, and someone keeps being there, every fall, every age. ...you've got the knack, climber. You'd know. Were you there? The strata thinks you were."

"Mordathun's dead, the strata's clear on that — no pulse in the pressure, no breath in the bands, whatever Doun feels at his crack, the rock says dead. But dead and gone are different words, climber, and the Old Weight is one and not the other, and that's the band that should worry you: dead, vast, and still load-bearing. We live on it. We build on it. We kneel to it. Dead gods are the only foundation Titanfall's ever had."

titanfall.name: Outcast-Welcomer Vrenna Saltscree
titanfall.role: Mortal oddball / runs a halfway-house for the clanless
barks: "Clans cast you out? For building? For hurrying? For cheating the slow way? ...sit down, climber. I don't care what you did. The clans care enough for everyone. Somebody should keep a fire for the ones the mountain spat out. I'm somebody. This is the fire. There's stew. The stew doesn't judge. The stew's the most Stoneblooded thing left, and the clans won't claim it."

"R999 came through here, you know — Driftblood, the bitter one. Proud, clanless, furious. I fed him. He spat in the stew and left. Came back a month later and finished the bowl. They all come back. Bitterness makes you hungry, climber. Exile makes you hungry. The mountain makes everyone hungry, eventually. I just keep the pot on."

"You'll choose, one day — the slow way, true and clan-blessed, or the fast way, yours and exiled. And whichever you choose, the other path's people will hate you for it. ...but my fire's here for both. The only fire in Titanfall that is. Remember it, climber. You might be clanless yet. Most climbers are. The mountain's a hard clan to join and an easy one to fall out of."

titanfall.name: Stonewright B403 Deephand
barks: "Bond-gear. Forged slow, lasts long, helps the gentle path. The Iron Guild would laugh at the pace of it. The Iron Guild's gear rusts. Mine's outlived three of them."
"You want the rare-recessive boost? It's in the bloodline, not the gear — but the gear helps you wait. And waiting, child, is the whole craft. The whole clan."
"The mountain's a dead Titan. You're forging in its ribcage. Show some respect. The Old Weight remembers disrespect. It remembers everything. It's got nothing else to do but remember."

titanfall.name: The Herd-Singer, Granny Loam
barks: "Sit, sit. I'll sing you the line of the Worldback — Sproutling to Spiked-shell to apex, six generations of patience in every verse. You can't catch a song like that, child. You have to raise it."
"The fast ones — the Lab-makers, the catalyst-drinkers — they burn so bright. Then they're gone. The clans abide. We're the ash that stays warm. There's worse things to be. I've been worse things."

"The Old Weight stirs lately. The Titan's not waking — it's too dead for that. But it's dreaming. And its dreams have teeth. Mind the deep slopes, child. Bring a bonded beast. Bring patience. Bring me if I'm not too old, which I am."

titanfall.name: Tame-Warden Cuff Stillblood
barks: "Don't reach for it. Let it reach for you. Takes longer. Takes forever, some of them. The ones worth having are the forever ones."
"You catch with a trap, that's yours but it's not with you. You catch with a bond, it'd die for you. Different word. Different animal. Different you."

"Raise it here in Titanfall and the ground tints it Gaia — heavier, slower, truer. Environmental gene-expression, the Lab-folk call it. We just call it home getting into them. Same thing. Nicer word."

titanfall.name: The Last Titan-Priest, Mund Graveweight
barks: "I tend the shrine of a Titan whose name is lost. Older than the Olympians. Older than the factions. It fell so long ago it became the ground. I'm the last who kneels. Someone should. It was a god, once. It deserves a witness."

"The Olympians think they're eternal. The Titans thought so too. This one's a mountain now. The Old Weight is a lesson, climber, and the lesson is: you're next. Everyone's next. The throne is just a taller grave."

"You'll be a god, I can see it. Then you'll fall, they all fall, and become somewhere. I'll be long dead. But the next last priest will tend your corpse. ...it's a comfort. It's the only one the Old Weight offers. I've made my peace with it. You will too. Everyone does, eventually. Usually too late."

titanfall.name: Clanless R999 Driftblood
barks: "The clans cast me out. Said I used the Lab. Said I cheated. As if patience is a virtue and not just slowness with a flattering name. You take shortcuts too, climber. I can smell it. We're the same."
"Ostrega calls it 'the slow way.' I call it dying before you finish. I didn't have six generations. I had one life. So I built. They exiled me for wanting it in my lifetime."

"You'll choose too, eventually. Slow and true, or fast and mine. Choose fast and the clans hate you like they hate me. Choose slow and you'll die before the throne. ...I'm not bitter. I'm clanless. There's a difference. There's got to be."

verdant_glut.name: Greenmother Saoirse Lateharvest, Who Buries the Hungry
barks: "You've got blood under your nails and I can smell which kind. We don't do that here. But you came in instead of around — so. Tea?"
"You spared one you could've harvested. I saw your face do the math and then refuse it. That refusal is the whole faith, little one. Welcome to the losing side of it."
"You mend more than you maim now. The Glut feels it — the blooms lean your way. Walk the deep grove; the gentle things there have learned to fear footsteps, and they don't fear yours."
