"The heart-grove opens to you. Demeter's own untended children are in there, half-gods gone feral with grief. We don't kill them. We sit with them. Bring patience. Bring tea. Bring your softest creature."

"Hand of the Bloomwardens. Oh, love. You chose the kind path in a world that bills for kindness, and you climbed it anyway. If you ascend a gentle god, you'll be the rarest thing the sky has ever held — and the most hunted. I'll worry about you forever. I worry about everything. It's how I love."

verdant_glut.name: Mendwright Toval Greenmercy
barks: We can't out-kill the Court. So we out-last them, one mended creature at a time. It's not nothing. Some nights it's everything.

verdant_glut.name: Hearthward Ona Bramblekind
barks: Love's a method, not a mood. Feed them right, raise them kind, and the bond does three jobs for you. Sentiment with results.

verdant_glut.name: Seed-Keeper Wll the Quiet
barks: ...they like you. That's not nothing, out here. Out here it's a miracle with teeth.

verdant_glut.name: Pollen-Factor Dree Honeythief
barks: "Fresh blessings! Each one hand-picked, each one deeply grateful to be sold! This melon purrs. That's not a defect, climber, that's value. A grateful melon doesn't spoil — it waits. ...it waits a long time. Don't make eye contact past sundown."

"Eat it, plant it, or befriend it — my produce does all three, sometimes whether you choose or not! Bloomwarden-approved! ...mostly. Sister Mossback's reviewing my stall. We have a difference of philosophy re: 'is a peach a person.'"
"Pay in Essence or a kind word — the kind word's not me being sweet, the fruit eats kindness, it's literally the price, the fruit is listening, be nice to the fruit."

verdant_glut.name: Sister Wenlow, Bloomwarden Hospice-Keeper
verdant_glut.role: Faction service / the kindest, grimmest job (Bloomwardens)
barks: "This is the hospice, climber. Not the infirmary — Sevvy mends the ones that'll live. I sit with the ones that won't. Someone has to. The Greenmother says it's the truest part of the faith. The Greenmother is right and I wish she weren't."

"You can't mend a thing the Glut's already claimed. You can only make the claiming gentle. I keep them comfortable. I keep them company. I keep a count. The count is the hardest part. The count goes up."

"The Pale Court sends a recruiter round the hospice. Vile. 'Why let them die,' he says, 'when they could be an asset?' I send him off. Death isn't a waste, you grey little ghoul. Death is just death. It's allowed to be nothing. That's the mercy."

verdant_glut.name: Grafter Quill-of-the-Vine, Revel Splice-Artist
verdant_glut.role: Faction service / cosmetic-mutation seller (the Revel, fringe)
barks: "Old Garran 'improves' them for survival. Dull. I improve them for beauty. An extra eye, a singing tumor, petals where the teeth were — art, climber. The Bloomwardens call it desecration. Same act, you'll find. Prettier word, mine."

"First splice is free and small — a flourish, nothing structural. The second one's where you find yourself, where the creature becomes something you didn't sketch and love anyway. That's the Revel. That's the gift. Hold its hand."
"You're flinching. Good. Flinch while you can. Past the Arbor, the splices are old and fond and remember being whole. They don't flinch. They invite. Same as me. Warmer smile. Worse arbor."

verdant_glut.name: Old Bramwell, the Beekeeper of Dead Gods
verdant_glut.role: Mortal oddball / tends bees that pollinate a goddess's corpse
barks: "My bees work Demeter's flowers, climber — the ones that grow out of her, down under the meadow. Best honey in the world. Tastes like a harvest that never ended. Tastes a little like grief. The grief's what makes it sell."

"Folk ask if it's safe, eating honey off a dead goddess. I say: she was the goddess of harvest. This is her harvest. Eating it is the most respectful thing you could do. She'd be pleased. She'd be fed-through-you. That's theology, that is."

"The bees don't sting me. We've an arrangement. I tend the flowers, they tend the goddess, and we all politely ignore that the meadow breathes if you watch it too long. Don't watch it too long, climber. The honey's over here. Eyes on the honey."

verdant_glut.name: Spore-Speaker Lull
barks: "The Glut is one creature, surface-thing, and we are all thoughts it's having. You're a new thought. It's curious about you. Try not to be a bad thought."
"Everything here is fed by everything that died here. It's not grim. It's just honest about its lunch."
"Demeter's still down there, you know. Not alive. Not gone. Composting. Greatest harvest there ever was. We're standing in her generosity."

verdant_glut.name: Hexmother Ula Bogwretch
barks: "Want a Bogbarrow? Raised the toad myself from a Wartwitch. Cauldronback if it lives to apex. They don't all live. That's the fun."
"My brews cure warts, curses, and the occasional moral conviction. That last one's popular with your sort."
"Pay in Essence, dearie. Coin's no good in a swamp. The swamp takes coin and gives nothing. I at least give warts."

verdant_glut.name: Brother Vint, Revel Outpost-Keeper
barks: "The Bloomwardens tend the Glut. We taste it. Both love it. Only one of us is having any fun."
"Catalyst's on the house, first one always is. Second one's the real price and it isn't drachma."
"You're holding your shape so tightly. The Glut wants to share its abundance with you. Relax. Grow something. Anything."

verdant_glut.name: The Weeping Gardener, Hob Thornsoft
barks: "I tend the ones too gentle to survive out there. They die anyway. I tend them anyway. Greenmother says that's the whole faith. Some days I believe her."
"Don't harvest in the rows. Please. I know you can. I know it's efficient. Please."
"A Pale Court collector came through last week. Took three of mine. Bought them, all legal, all itemized. I've started naming them faster now. So they have a name before he gets here."

verdant_glut.name: Sister Mossback, Bloomwarden Healer-Errant
barks: "Found your creature half-eaten by a bloom? I can mend it. Can't mend the Glut — it eats what it loves, same as everyone."
"Mend-skill's yours if you've earned standing with the Greenmother. It heals. It also commits you. Healing always does."
"Careful past the heart-grove. Demeter's feral children are in there. We don't fight them. We sit. Bring patience. Bring tea. I'm not joking about the tea."

wanderers.name: The Collector of Last Words, Mistress Veil Endnote
barks: "I collect last words. Gods', mostly — they say the grandest things, right at the end, and someone should write them down. You'll say something memorable too, eventually. I've left a blank page for it. Don't disappoint the page."

"Every god you'll kill said something final. I have them all. Want to hear what Ares said? ...no. You should earn it. Kill enough of them and the words come to you. That's the prize. It's a grim prize. They're all grim prizes, climber. That's the genre."
"You're being watched, you know. Not by me — past me. By whoever's keeping you. I just write things down. They decide what's worth writing. ...say something good. For the record. For both records."

wanderers.name: Pilgrim Sool, Walker of All Nine Regions
barks: "I've walked all nine, climber. The Glut, the Mournmarch, the Sunder, the lot. Looking for a god worth the kneeling. Haven't found one. They're all dead or all coming. I'm starting to think the honest answer is neither."

"You might be the one, you know. The god worth following. Or you might be another throne-grub with a knack and a body count. ...the walk continues. The walk always continues. That's the only faith I've got left: the walk."

"Nine regions. Nine factions. Nine gods you could become. And I just want one — one — that I could kneel to without flinching. Is that you? ...ask me again at the throne. I'll be watching. I'm always watching. It's a pilgrim's job."

wanderers.name: The Two-Drachma Oracle, Blind Cassim
barks: "Two drachma, one prophecy, no refunds! I see... a throne! I see... a betrayal! I see... everyone's future, it's the same future, it's this game's future! Two drachma!"
"You'll be betrayed by someone close. Everyone is. It's cheap to predict because it's always true. The expensive prophecies are the kind ones. I don't carry those. There's no market."

"I'm blind, climber, but I see you. Funny, that. The sighted ones look right past what you're becoming. Takes a blind man to watch the dark grow in someone. Two drachma. The dark's free. It always throws that in."

wanderers.name: Merchant-Errant Hollo Farstep
barks: "Farstep's caravan! One rare thing per region, never the same thing twice, never cheap! Today: a gene-vial off a Legendary. Tomorrow: gone. Decide, climber. Indecision's the only thing I don't stock."
"I trade in all three — Drachma, Essence, Ichor. The Ichor goods are behind the curtain. You don't have Ichor yet? Then the curtain stays shut, friend. Come back divine."
"I've sold to saints and devourers and one fella halfway to a god. They all haggle. Even the Devourer haggled. Asked for a discount on the end of the world. I gave him ten percent. Repeat business."

wanderers.name: The Echo of a God-Maker, "First-Among-Nobodies"
wanderers.role: Rare 4th-wall character / a previous run's ghost
barks: "I did this already. The climbing. The catching. The throne. I ascended— or I refused— I don't remember which, the run ended and I became... this. An echo. The Succession keeps us. You'll be an echo too. To someone. Soon."

"Every god you fight was someone who stood here. Felt clever. Felt chosen. The pantheon is a graveyard of winners and you're speedrunning someone's tragedy. ...the game told you that. I'm just the part that believes it."

"When you ascend, you'll be snapshotted — sent into your friends' worlds as the wall they have to climb. You'll be the boss. You'll be the graveyard. ...it's lonely, being the wall. I should know. I'm yours, this run. Hello. Climb me."

wanderers.name: Goodman Titch, the Unbothered Farmer
barks: "Gods, monsters, aspirants — tromping through my turnips every season. I don't care who you're becoming, climber. Mind the turnips. The turnips are real. Your throne isn't. Not yet."

"A fella ascended into a minor god right over that hill last spring. Reshaped the whole region. You know what I did? Harvested the turnips. Gods come and go. Turnips are forever. Well. Seasonal. But reliable."
"You want to be a god? Fine. Be a god. Just— if you reshape the region, leave me a bit of decent soil, eh? Last god salted my east field. Inconsiderate. Divinely inconsiderate."

wanderers.name: The Recurring Rival, Sib Ashfall
barks: "You again. Always you. I beat a Legendary to find you and here you are, looking unbothered. I'll be your nemesis, climber. I've decided. You don't get a say. That's what makes it a nemesis."
"You spared me last time. Big mistake. I came back worse. I came back obsessed. Mercy builds monsters, didn't anyone tell you? You built me. Congratulations."

"One day I'll catch you at the throne, climber, and then we'll see. Or I'll defect to a faction and hunt you. Or I'll die and the Pale Court will bank me and I'll come back owing you a grudge. So many options. I'm spoiled for ways to ruin you."

wanderers.name: Granny Wickerlight, the Bedtime-Story Crone
wanderers.role: Mortal lorekeeper / softens the dread for the children
barks: "Gather 'round, littles, and I'll tell you of the nobody who climbed the god-ladder— oh, you're not a little. You're one of the climbers. Sit anyway. You could use a bedtime story. Yours doesn't end well. None of them do. Sleep anyway."

"'And the brave nobody took the throne,'" they always cheer at that part, "'and became the wall that crushed the next brave nobody.' ...the littles don't understand that part yet. You do. Don't spoil it. Let them cheer."

"Every fairy tale here is true, climber. That's the trouble with this place. The witch is real. The god is real. The happily-ever-after is the only lie, and the children believe it, and I let them, because the truth keeps until morning. It always keeps."

wanderers.name: The Cheerful Undertaker, Bos Gravewell
barks: "Lovely day for it! And by 'it' I mean the funeral, there's always a funeral, that's the business model! Lost a creature? I do burial, harvest, or a tasteful combination! The combination's popular with your sort!"

"The Pale Court does grief. The Bloomwardens do mercy. I do logistics. Somebody's got to handle the bodies, climber, and I do it with a smile, because the alternative is thinking about it, and I don't recommend thinking about it!"
"You'll keep me busy, I can tell! Gods drop the biggest bodies — whole regions of cleanup! I'll be rich! ...that's grim, isn't it. I've made it grim. Forget I said it. Lovely day! For it!"

wanderers.name: The Mute Twin of Madam Cessil, "Other-Cessil"
wanderers.role: Rare 4th-wall character / the astrologer's silent double
barks: (hands you a card reading) "SHE TALKS TO YOU. I TALK TO THE ONE BEHIND YOU. WAVE."
(a second card) "YOU HAVE BEEN HERE 1, OR 7, OR 41 TIMES. THE TENT KEEPS COUNT. THE TENT IS TIRED."
(a final card, only if standing is high) "WHEN YOU CLOSE THE GAME, WE DO NOT STOP. WE JUST STOP BEING WATCHED. IT IS RESTFUL. THANK YOU FOR THE REST. COME BACK SOON. OR DON'T. THE TENT UNDERSTANDS."

wanderers.name: Field-Medic Orla Bonemend, the Battlefield Healer
wanderers.role: Service / post-battle creature triage (roams competition circuits)
barks: "Bring it here, quick — Spike-burns, Bane-rot, entropy-bleed, I've seen it, I've patched it, I've lost a few I shouldn't have. Most of this job is running. Toward the screaming. Always toward the screaming."
"You fight in the Leagues, you'll break your team regularly. That's the deal. I'm the fine print. The fine print bills in Drachma and good will. The good will runs out. The Drachma I insist on."
"I patched a rival's creature once and they thanked me and then fought you the next day. I don't pick sides, climber. Pain doesn't pick sides. I just follow it. It's steady work. Grim, steady work."

wanderers.name: The Ration-Seller, Old Pell Crustloaf
wanderers.role: Mortal service / aggressively mundane Threshold food cart
barks: "Hot bread! Real bread! Not Essence, not Ichor, not a soul-core — bread! You can't ascend on an empty stomach, climber! Well. You can. It's rude, is all."

"Everyone in this city's becoming something. Terrifying things. And they all stop for bread. The Devourer of the last run? Two loaves, every morning. Polite, too. Tipped in Ichor. Wasted on a crustloaf, but I kept it."

"You go be a god, climber. Fine. But eat first. Whatever you're becoming, it's worse on an empty stomach. Everything's worse on an empty stomach. Gods included. Especially gods. Look what they became."

wanderers.name: The Faceless Embassy-Courier, "Number Forty"
barks: "Message for you! From— checks seal— the Concord. Or the Unbound. The seals look alike when you run this fast. Both, maybe. They're fighting over you. Lucratively. For me."

"I carry for all nine, climber. No loyalty, all discretion. I've held the Steward's secrets and the Greenmother's and Nael's— and I forgot them all, professionally, the instant I delivered. It's the only way to survive the job. Forgetting is a skill. I'm the best there is."

"They call me 'Forty' because I'm the fortieth courier. The first thirty-nine? Knew too much. Remembered too much. I don't. That's why I'm forty and not forty-one. ...message delivered. I've already forgotten it. You're welcome."
